title: A Weather for the Inventory
premise: Lior Kavanagh, a celebrated restaurant critic who lost her sense of taste after her brother's death, has spent nine years cataloguing the words her family never said in a private inventory of grief. At her mother's funeral, a stranger named Ada greets the family as 'the Bellamys' — a name from a life before Lior was born — and reveals she holds letters that could rewrite everything Lior believes about her father's disappearance. Returning to the shuttered family inn on the coast where it all went wrong, Lior must piece together the truth: her father didn't abandon them; he was sent away to protect a secret about her own parentage, and Ada is his daughter. As the inn faces demolition and her memory begins to fail like her palate did, Lior must choose between preserving the inventory of unsaid things or finally saying them. In the end she reopens the inn's kitchen, cooks one meal she can't taste but can finally feel, and gives the Bellamy name back to the sea.
about_author: Juniper Fairweather is the pen name of a former line cook turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing ephemera in coastal New England historical societies. She writes about food, forgetting, and the families we assemble from what survives.

chapters.title: The Inventory
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. We meet her at a tasting menu she cannot taste, professionally describing flavors she no longer perceives, then home to her notebooks of unsaid things. Establishes her ritualized grief and her brother Danny's absence beneath everything. Emotional beat: controlled numbness cracking at the edges.

chapters.title: A Funeral in Good Weather
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Her mother's funeral is oddly cheerful; her surviving relatives perform closeness badly. Then Ada, a woman in her fifties, embraces Lior's aunt and calls them 'the Bellamys.' No one corrects her. Lior watches her family flinch in unison. Emotional beat: the first hairline fracture in the official story.

chapters.title: What the Stranger Left Behind
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Ada leaves without explanation but slips a photograph into the condolence book: the family inn, intact, with a man Lior doesn't recognize standing beside her father. Lior confronts her aunt Ruth, who shuts down hard. Emotional beat: curiosity sharpening into obsession.

chapters.title: Tongue Memory
chapters.summary: Alternating POV: flashbacks to young Lior and Danny cooking with their father at the inn before he vanished. Present-day Lior realizes her taste died the same week her father's letters stopped coming. She books a ticket to the coast. Emotional beat: grief given a geography.

chapters.title: The House That Kept Its Name
chapters.summary: Lior arrives at the derelict inn, slated for demolition in six weeks. The town remembers 'the Bellamys' fondly and the Kavanaghs not at all. She breaks in through the kitchen door and finds her childhood preserved under dust. Emotional beat: uncanny homecoming, tenderness laced with dread.

chapters.title: Ada at the Door
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada has been watching the inn too; she grew up hearing about it. She catches Lior inside and instead of calling the police, makes tea on a camp stove. Two guarded women circle each other over shared crockery. Emotional beat: wary alliance forming over something warm.

chapters.title: Letters, Sealed
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Ada produces a bundle of letters her late grandmother kept — correspondence between Lior's father and a woman who was not Lior's mother. Lior reads three lines and stops, unable to continue. Emotional beat: the inventory of unsaid things meets its first said thing.

chapters.title: Danny's Room
chapters.summary: Lior's POV, alone at night. She finds Danny's old room untouched since his death and confronts the second grief she's been inventorying around: her brother drowned off the inn's dock at nineteen, weeks before their father left. Emotional beat: the two losses revealed as one wound.

chapters.title: The Town Remembers Differently
chapters.summary: Multiple small POVs: the fishmonger, the retired postmistress, a barman. Each offers a fragment — the father was seen the night Danny drowned; the mother paid someone to stay quiet; the name change happened fast. Emotional beat: communal memory as an unreliable chorus.

chapters.title: Ruth Comes Down the Hill
chapters.summary: Ruth's POV. Aunt Ruth arrives to drag Lior home and finds her living at the inn. Their fight cracks open Ruth's guilt: she helped Lior's mother change the name and bury the letters. Emotional beat: anger transmuting into shared shame.

chapters.title: Half a Recipe
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. In the inn's kitchen she finds her father's recipe book, pages torn out. Cooking from the remaining recipes, she experiences phantom taste for the first time in nine years — sensation without flavor. Ada helps her cook. Emotional beat: hope arriving through the hands, not the tongue.

chapters.title: The Other Daughter
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Ada confesses: the letters are between her grandmother and Lior's father, and Ada believes she is his daughter — Lior's half-sister. Lior's world tilts. She walks into the cold sea up to her knees. Emotional beat: betrayal and relief braided together.

chapters.title: Inventory, Interrupted
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She rereads her notebooks and sees how the inventory itself became a way of never living. She burns nothing but stops writing. A demolition notice appears on the inn door — the timeline accelerates. Emotional beat: turning point; grief's architecture deliberately dismantled.

chapters.title: What the Mother Knew
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, mother's POV, written in second person. The night Danny drowned, the father chose to stay with the dying boy rather than call for help in time — or so the mother believed — and she exiled him rather than forgive him, taking the children and a new name. Emotional beat: tragic misunderstanding laid bare.

chapters.title: The Torn Pages
chapters.summary: Lior and Ada search the inn for the missing recipe pages and find them lining a drawer in Danny's room — hidden by Danny himself, meaning he knew about Ada's existence before he died. Emotional beat: the dead brother becomes an active presence, almost a co-conspirator.

chapters.title: Storm Warning
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. A storm approaches; the demolition crew moves up its schedule; Ruth returns having found the father alive in a care facility two towns over, his mind going. Time is running out on every clock at once. Emotional beat: rising panic, all threads converging.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Both Names
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. She visits her father. He doesn't always know her, but when she says 'Bellamy,' he surfaces, and he tells her the truth of Danny's death — he wasn't negligent; he made an impossible choice trying to save him. Emotional beat: devastating absolution, forgiveness arriving decades late and still warm.

chapters.title: One Meal, Said Aloud
chapters.summary: Lior and Ada cook the completed recipe — the dish Danny loved — in the inn's kitchen while the storm hits. Lior speaks every unsaid thing from her inventory aloud to the empty dining room, naming each entry and releasing it. Emotional beat: climax; catharsis performed as liturgy.

chapters.title: What the Sea Takes
chapters.summary: Storm's peak, alternating Lior/Ada. The demolition crew tries to board up early; the sisters defend the inn through the night, and part of it — the wing where Danny died — collapses into the sea anyway. They let it go. Emotional beat: acceptance as active surrender.

chapters.title: Aftertaste
chapters.summary: Lior's POV. Morning after. Standing in the ruined kitchen, Lior tastes salt on her lips and realizes the sense is returning — imperfect, unreliable, hers. She writes one final inventory entry: a list of things now said. Emotional beat: quiet resurrection.

chapters.title: The Bellamy Table
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV. Weeks later: the inn's core is saved as a community kitchen; Ruth signs the papers; their father moves to a room upstairs; Ada stays. The first public dinner is served to the town, everyone who once gave testimony now seated at one table. Emotional beat: found family formalized in flour and steam.

chapters.title: A Weather for the Inventory
chapters.summary: Lior's final POV. She reviews a restaurant again — honestly this time, tasting everything, including the memory in it. On the last page she closes the old inventory notebook and opens a blank one titled only with tomorrow's date. Emotional beat: resolution; grief integrated, appetite restored, story handed forward.
